name: chai-persistent-numeric-distribution-a98e
instr:
Chai cannot collect durable numeric column statistics or use observed selectivity to choose indexes. Add SQL ANALYZE support while preserving native INTEGER, BIGINT, and DOUBLE PRECISION ordering through collection, persistence, and planning.

Every Numeric implementation must compute deterministic finite-range positions in its native domain. Positions stay monotonic without overflow or precision loss. Signed zeros compare as zero. Reversed ranges return ErrInvalidDistributionRange with exact text "invalid distribution range". For a degenerate range, a value below both bounds returns position 0, a value equal to both bounds returns position 1, and a value above both bounds returns position 2, without dividing by zero. NewIntegerNumeric(x) and NewBigintNumeric(x) validate boundaries and agree for equivalent exact values.

ANALYZE atomically publishes deterministic equi-depth distributions accounting for every visible row through row, null, finite, NaN, and infinity counts. Committed summaries retain typed bounds, buckets, counts, encoded ordering, and generations after reopening. Committed mutations make them stale; rollback exposes neither mutations nor replacement summaries. ColumnStatistics.Fresh() reports generation agreement. (*Catalog).ColumnStatistics(tableName, columnName) (ColumnStatistics, bool) returns the stored summary and availability.

Equality and ordered estimates must be deterministic, bounded, frequency-aware, and monotonic as ranges widen. Finite matches ex
